Prompt title: If you have engaged in significant research in the natural sciences
Why: Asks for a description of an independent research project - a sustained project, described.
Full written prompt: If you have engaged in significant research in the natural sciences, mathematics, computer science, social sciences or humanities that was undertaken independently of your high school curriculum, please provide a brief description of the research project.

Prompt title: If you would like to share more about yourself that is not captured
Why: Literally open topic: anything about yourself not captured elsewhere. The rare genuine case.
Full written prompt: If you would like to share more about yourself that is not captured elsewhere in your application, please tell us more here.

Prompt title: Option A: Curiosity
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: “Hope and curiosity — these are qualities that are the foundation of what Amherst College means, of everything that we do here. Curiosity is at the core of a liberal arts education — a spirit of inquiry that shapes not only what our students do in the classroom, but also how they learn from and about each other.” — Michael A. Elliott, 20th President of Amherst College, address at Amherst College’s 203rd Commencement What does curiosity mean to you? How do you experience curiosity in your own life?

Prompt title: Option A: Disagreement and connection
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: “We are working together to build a community that makes room for both true disagreement and true connection, one that practices the kind of recognition and robust negotiation that the everyday life of democracy requires, and one that explicitly prepares our students to work for the greater good in their professional and personal endeavors.” — Presidential Priorities: Serving the Greater Good Tell us about a time that you engaged with a viewpoint different from your own. How did you enter that engagement, and what did you learn about yourself from it?

Prompt title: Option A: Unique experiences
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: “We seek an Amherst made stronger because it includes those whose experiences can enhance our understanding of our nation and our world. We do so in the faith that our humanity is an identity forged from diversity, and that our different perspectives enrich our inquiry, deepen our knowledge, strengthen our community, and prepare students to engage with an ever-changing world.” — from the Trustee Statement on Diversity and Community In what ways could your unique experiences enhance our understanding of our nation and our world?

Prompt title: Please briefly elaborate on an extracurricular activity or work
Why: An extracurricular or work experience of particular significance - the activity family, asked for significance.
Full written prompt: Please briefly elaborate on an extracurricular activity or work experience of particular significance to you.

Prompt title: Tell us about a time when something did not go according to plan
Why: Something that did not go to plan and how you responded, tied to Barrett fit.
Full written prompt: Tell us about a time when something did not go according to plan. Focus less on the outcome and more on how the ways you responded in the moment suggest you are a strong fit for Barrett.

Prompt title: What is a question you find yourself returning to repeatedly
Why: A question you return to; bespoke intellectual framing tied to honours-college fit.
Full written prompt: What is a question you find yourself returning to repeatedly? How does your pursuit of an answer, or even just the persistence of the question itself, suggest you are a strong fit for Barrett?

Prompt title: What is an object that connects you to your family or community, and
Why: An object connecting you to family or community, and why - identity through an object.
Full written prompt: What is an object that connects you to your family or community, and how or why does it do this? How does this connection make you a strong fit for Barrett?

Prompt title: A meaningful conversation partner
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: The late BC theology professor, Father Michael Himes, argued that a university is not a place to which you go, but instead, a “rigorous and sustained conversation about the great questions of human existence, among the widest possible circle of the best possible conversation partners.” Who has been your most meaningful conversation partner, and what profound questions have you considered together?

Prompt title: A fourth 'Be'
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Boston College’s Jesuit mission highlights “the three Be’s”: be attentive, be reflective, be loving – core to Jesuit education (see A Pocket Guide to Jesuit Education). If you could add a fourth “Be,” what would it be and why? How would this new value support your personal development and enrich the BC community?

Prompt title: The danger of a single story
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: In her July 2009 Ted Talk, “The Danger of a Single Story,” Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie warned viewers against assigning people a “single story” through assumptions about their nationality, appearance, or background. Discuss a time when someone defined you by a single story. What challenges did this present and how did you overcome them?

Prompt title: A meaningful tradition
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Strong communities are sustained by traditions. Boston College’s annual calendar is marked with both long-standing and newer traditions that help shape our community. Tell us about a meaningful tradition in your family or community. Why is it important to you, and how does it bring people together or strengthen the bonds of those who participate?

Prompt title: Human-Centered Engineering and the Common Good
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: One goal of a Jesuit education is to prepare students to serve the Common Good. Human-Centered Engineering at Boston College integrates technical knowledge, creativity, and a humanistic perspective to address societal challenges and opportunities. What societal problems are important to you and how will you use your HCE education to solve them?

Prompt title: If you could create a new Kilachand course, what would it be
Why: Invent a Kilachand course aligned to Kilachand's values: institution-specific by construction.
Full written prompt: If you could create a new Kilachand course, what would it be? How would your imagined course align with the core values of Kilachand?

Prompt title: What about being a student at BU most excites you
Why: What excites you about being a BU student.
Full written prompt: What about being a student at BU most excites you?

Prompt title: What about the Kilachand Honors College resonates with you, and how
Why: What resonates about Kilachand and how its curriculum meets your goals.
Full written prompt: What about the Kilachand Honors College resonates with you, and how would Kilachand’s curriculum fulfill your academic, creative, intellectual, and/or professional goals?

Prompt title: How did you first learn about Bowdoin
Why: A one-line factual question about how you heard of Bowdoin.
Full written prompt: How did you first learn about Bowdoin?

Prompt title: Navigating through differences
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Bowdoin believes that its broadly diverse and inclusive campus community prepares graduates to be contributing and useful citizens of the world. Every graduate of this institution should be confident in their preparation to be able to navigate through differences and in all sorts of situations. A Bowdoin education does not guarantee these skills, but it does impart a set of tools necessary to bravely enter unfamiliar conditions with the confidence to deal effectively with ambiguity. If you wish, you may share anything about the unique experiences and perspectives that you would bring with you to the Bowdoin campus and community or an experience you have had that required you to navigate across or through difference.

Prompt title: The Offer of the College
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Generations of students have found connection and meaning in Bowdoin’s “The Offer of the College,” written in 1906 by Bowdoin President William DeWitt Hyde. To be at home in all lands and all ages; to count Nature a familiar acquaintance, and Art an intimate friend; to gain a standard for the appreciation of others’ work and the criticism of your own; to carry the keys of the world’s library in your pocket, and feel its resources behind you in whatever task you undertake; to make hosts of friends...who are to be leaders in all walks of life; to lose yourself in generous enthusiasms and cooperate with others for common ends— This is the offer of the college for the best four years of your life. Which line from The Offer resonates most with you? The Offer represents Bowdoin’s values. Please reflect on the line you selected and how it has meaning to you.

Prompt title: The Myra Kraft Transitional Year Program (MKTYP) / Achievers Program is
Why: Strengths you bring to a cohort and what you gain from others - future contribution to a group.
Full written prompt: The Myra Kraft Transitional Year Program (MKTYP) / Achievers Program is designed to guide you toward adjusting to the rigors and challenges of the college experience with a small cohort of peers. What strengths will you bring to the group, and in what areas will you benefit from the strengths of others?

Prompt title: What excites you the most about being an international student at
Why: What excites you about being an international student specifically at Brandeis.
Full written prompt: What excites you the most about being an international student at Brandeis University?

Prompt title: Brown | RISD Dual Degree
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: The Brown | RISD Dual Degree Program draws on the complementary strengths of Brown University and Rhode Island School of Design (RISD) to provide students with the opportunity to explore and engage with diverse spheres of academic and creative inquiry. Considering your understanding of the academic programs at Brown and RISD, describe how and why the specific blend of RISD’s experimental, immersive art and design program and Brown’s wide-ranging courses and curricula could constitute an optimal undergraduate education for you. Reflect on how you might integrate or synthesize content, approaches, and methods from these two distinct learning experiences. Additionally, how might you contribute to the Dual Degree community and its commitment to interdisciplinary work?

Prompt title: Growing up and contributing to Brown
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Students entering Brown often find that making their home on College Hill naturally invites reflection on where they came from. Share how an aspect of your growing up has inspired or challenged you, and what unique contributions this might allow you to make to the Brown community.

Prompt title: What brings you joy
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Brown students care deeply about their work and the world around them. Students find contentment, satisfaction, and meaning in daily interactions and major discoveries. Whether big or small, mundane or spectacular, tell us about something that brings you joy.

Prompt title: Your approach to the Open Curriculum
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: “There is something distinctive about Brown students. It is a blend of intellectual curiosity, creativity, and humility. A commitment to collaboration. An openness to new ideas and perspectives. A desire to make the world better. And it is resilience: the ability to recover and thrive after experiencing difficulties.” From President Christina Paxson’s 2025 Convocation Address. How will you use these characteristics or others to shape your approach to the Open Curriculum?

Prompt title: Teach a class
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: If you could teach a class on any one thing, whether academic or otherwise, what would it be?

Prompt title: PLME: What will make you a great doctor?
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Tell us something about yourself, beyond your interest in medicine, that you think will make you a great doctor.

Prompt title: PLME: Why medicine?
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Why medicine?

Prompt title: PLME: Why PLME?
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Why PLME?

Prompt title: Please explain your interest in your first-choice major/undecided
Why: Interest in a first and second choice major, and why Bucknell for it.
Full written prompt: Please explain your interest in your first-choice major/undecided status and your second-choice major (should you opt to list one) and why you would choose Bucknell University to pursue your interest(s).

Prompt title: Required STEM Academic Interest
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Why did you choose your proposed area of interest? If you selected ‘other’, what topics are you interested in pursuing?

Prompt title: Fun Question
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Caltech students bring more than academic ability to the communities they join. What is something you would be excited to do, share, teach, make, start, or contribute as part of the Caltech community?

Prompt title: Optional Academic Context
Why: carried over from the hand review
Word limit: (note) The source states no word or character limit.
Full written prompt: Caltech cares about context. Is there anything about your academic preparation, coursework, school context, or learning experiences that would help us better understand your readiness for Caltech?

Prompt title: Scholarly Character: Collaboration
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Tell us about a time your learning in STEM was shaped by another person or group — either because you needed help, offered help, changed your thinking through collaboration, or contributed to someone else’s understanding. What did that experience teach you about learning and working with others?

Prompt title: Scholarly Character: Process
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Tell us about a time your approach to a STEM problem, concept, or project mattered as much as the outcome. How did you work through uncertainty or persist creatively in tackling the problem? What would you still defend about your process, regardless of the outcome?

Prompt title: Scientific Drive: Learning
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Regardless of your STEM interest listed above, take this opportunity to nerd out and talk to us about whatever STEM rabbit hole you have found yourself falling into. Be as specific or broad as you would like.

Prompt title: Scientific Drive: Making
Why: AUDIT: something you created, repaired, coded or built, and what the process revealed. Was Other, while Cornell's and Tufts' near-identical make-something prompts are Activities & Impact.
Full written prompt: Tell us about something you created, tested, repaired, modeled, coded, built, or redesigned. What problem were you trying to solve and what did the process reveal to you?

Prompt title: Scientific Drive: Pursuing
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Tell us about a STEM question, problem, idea, or project that has held your attention over time. What drew you to it, how have you pursued it, and what do you still want to understand?

Prompt title: Anything missing
Why: The additional-information box: fill any gaps, any topic.
Word limit: (note) The source states no word or character limit.
Full written prompt: Anything missing? Do you want to share more with us? If so, use this space to fill any gaps you think would assist us in reviewing your application.

Prompt title: Think about someone you connect with who’s different from you
Why: Someone different from you and what is meaningful in those interactions - engaging across difference.
Full written prompt: Think about someone you connect with who’s different from you. What do you find most meaningful about your interactions with them?

Prompt title: What you want to emphasize
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Consider your application as a whole. What do you personally want to emphasize about your application for the admission committee’s consideration? Highlight something that’s important to you or something you haven’t had a chance to share. Tell us, don’t show us (no websites please).

Prompt title: Passion behind your intended area of study
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Most students choose their intended major or area of study based on a passion or inspiration that’s developed over time — what passion or inspiration led you to choose this area of study?

Prompt title: A successful college experience
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Many students pursue college for a specific degree, career opportunity or personal goal. Whichever it may be, learning will be critical to achieve your ultimate goal. As you think ahead to the process of learning during your college years, how will you define a successful college experience?

Prompt title: By applying to the Pre-Professional Scholars Program, you are applying
Why: Why this profession, how you are suited, and what led you there.
Full written prompt: By applying to the Pre-Professional Scholars Program, you are applying to gain admission to professional school earlier than students who apply in the traditional way. Please indicate why you’re interested in your chosen profession. How do you see yourself being particularly suited to this field? What events and/or experiences have led you to your choice?

Prompt title: In the college application process, you are constantly prompted for a
Why: Something you are proud of that appears nowhere else - deliberately not an activity listing.
Full written prompt: In the college application process, you are constantly prompted for a list of your achievements, awards, and accomplishments. While this information is useful to us, we are interested in hearing more about you. Describe an event, achievement, or experience of which you are particularly proud but that will not show up on a resume, may not garner any recognition, and does not appear anywhere else on your admission application.

Prompt title: Open Academy and constructive dialogue
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: A critical part of fulfilling our mission is living out the commitments of CMC’s Open Academy: Freedom of Expression, Viewpoint Diversity, and Constructive Dialogue. We want to learn more about your commitment to listening and learning from others with different viewpoints, perspectives, and life experiences from your own. Describe a time when engaging with someone about a specific topic resulted in you changing your attitude, belief, or behavior, or you changed the belief or behavior of someone else. What was the change that occurred for you, and what facilitated that change? What did you learn from that experience, and how has it informed how you engage with others?

Prompt title: Why Claremont McKenna
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: CMC’s mission is to prepare students for thoughtful and productive lives and responsible leadership in business, government, and the professions. With this mission in mind, please explain why you want to attend Claremont McKenna College.

Prompt title: Colgate students immerse themselves in social and intellectual pursuits
Why: What inspires you and why you want to pursue it at Colgate.
Full written prompt: Colgate students immerse themselves in social and intellectual pursuits that inspire them. Tell us in 250 words or less what inspires you and why you want to pursue that at Colgate.

Prompt title: On Colgate’s campus, students engage with individuals from a variety of
Why: The benefits you see in engaging with a diverse campus, forward-looking.
Full written prompt: On Colgate’s campus, students engage with individuals from a variety of socioeconomic backgrounds, races, ethnicities, religions, and perspectives during the course of their educational and social experiences. In 250 words or less, please share the benefits you see in engaging with a diverse body of students, faculty, and staff as part of your Colgate experience.

Prompt title: Please complete the following so we can learn a bit more about you
Why: Thirteen sentence stems at 13 words each: the short-form list format.
Full written prompt: Please complete the following so we can learn a bit more about you. Each response should be no more than 13 words. 1. I am fascinated by… 2. My favorite book, movie, or television show is… 3. The person I admire most is… 4. In the future, I hope to… 5. One historical figure I would like to meet is… 6. My favorite food is… 7. One thing I would change is… 8. My favorite place is… 9. I am the best version of myself when… 10. Something that has changed my perspective is… 11. I am seeking a community that… 12. My favorite family/community/cultural tradition is… 13. I am drawn to Colgate University because…

Prompt title: The luxury of focus
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: One of the benefits of Colorado College’s Block Plan is the opportunity to immerse yourself fully in a single subject for 3.5 weeks. We see this as the luxury of focus—the joy and value of directing your full attention to one thing. Tell us about a time when you experienced this kind of deep focus in an academic or extracurricular setting. What were you doing, and how did it turn out?

Prompt title: At Columbia, students representing a wide range of perspectives are
Why: A time you disagreed and what you took away - filed as Harvard's and Amherst's disagreement prompts are.
Full written prompt: At Columbia, students representing a wide range of perspectives are invited to live and learn together. In such a community, questions and debates naturally arise. Please describe a time when you did not agree with someone and discuss how you engaged with them and what you took away from the interaction.

Prompt title: In college/university, students are often challenged in ways that they
Why: Navigating adversity and how you changed as a result.
Full written prompt: In college/university, students are often challenged in ways that they could not anticipate. Please describe a situation in which you have navigated through adversity and discuss how you changed as a result.

Prompt title: List the titles of texts, resources and outlets that have contributed
Why: List the titles of texts and outlets: a list of works, not an essay about them.
Full written prompt: List the titles of texts, resources and outlets that have contributed to your intellectual development outside of academic courses, including but not limited to books, journals, websites, podcasts, essays, plays, presentations, videos, museums and other content that you enjoy.

Prompt title: Tell us about an aspect of your life so far or your lived experience
Why: Lived experience and how it shapes what you would contribute at Columbia.
Full written prompt: Tell us about an aspect of your life so far or your lived experience that is important to you, and describe how it has shaped the way you would learn from and contribute to Columbia's multidimensional and collaborative environment.

Prompt title: What attracts you to your preferred areas of study at Columbia College
Why: What attracts you to your preferred areas of study.
Full written prompt: What attracts you to your preferred areas of study at Columbia College or Columbia Engineering?

Prompt title: Why are you interested in attending Columbia University
Why: Why Columbia, explicitly about what is unique to it.
Full written prompt: Why are you interested in attending Columbia University? We encourage you to consider the aspect(s) that you find unique and compelling about Columbia.

Prompt title: At the College of Arts and Sciences, your education is yours to shape
Why: An intellectual passion plus which parts of the liberal arts curriculum you would draw on.
Full written prompt: At the College of Arts and Sciences, your education is yours to shape. Describe an intellectual passion, question, or idea that has captured your attention—whether it emerges from your studies or extends beyond your coursework. What specific aspects of our liberal arts curriculum would you draw on to explore and connect your varied interests?

Prompt title: Describe a fashion brand, retailer, product, campaign, resale platform
Why: A fashion object or campaign that changed your thinking, and the larger question it raised.
Full written prompt: Describe a fashion brand, retailer, product, campaign, resale platform, event, or consumer behavior that has made you think differently about the fashion industry. What did you notice, and what larger question did it raise for you about value, identity, labor, sustainability, technology, culture, or markets?

Prompt title: Describe how your interests connect to architecture
Why: How your interests connect to architecture, through a project that sparked it.
Full written prompt: Describe how your interests connect to architecture. Include an example of a creative project, design experience, or personal passion that sparked your interest in pursuing a 5-year professional degree in architecture. Reflect on how this experience shaped your understanding of the field and your motivation to study architecture.

Prompt title: Describe one garment, accessory, textile, image, or object that changed
Why: One garment or object and what you noticed about its form and meaning.
Full written prompt: Describe one garment, accessory, textile, image, or object that changed the way you think about fashion or design. What did you notice about its form, material, construction, proportion, movement, or meaning? BE specific about what you saw and why it stayed with you.

Prompt title: Describe your interest in urban and regional studies
Why: Interest in urban and regional studies and how Cornell's programme fits your goals.
Full written prompt: Describe your interest in urban and regional studies. Discuss experiences, ideas, or issues that have shaped your interest in cities, communities, and regional systems, and explain how URS at Cornell aligns with your academic and career goals.

Prompt title: Discuss your interest in pursuing a major in policy at the Cornell Jeb E
Proposed secondaries: Why Us; Activities & Impact; Values; Goals & Future
Final secondaries: Why Us; Values; Goals & Future; Activities & Impact
Why: Interest in policy, drawing on experience, values and activities.
Full written prompt: Discuss your interest in pursuing a major in policy at the Cornell Jeb E. Brooks School of Public Policy and what draws you to this field of study. You are encouraged to consider including details related to your personal experiences, values, academic influences, or extracurricular activities that have shaped your perspective and future goals.

Prompt title: Fashion design involves translating ideas into material form for real
Why: A critique of fashion you hope to explore through the major, and why it matters.
Full written prompt: Fashion design involves translating ideas into material form for real bodies, lives, and contexts, but it can fall short of those goals. Tell us about one critique of fashion that you hope to explore through fashion design, and why does it matter to you?

Prompt title: Fashion Design Management sits at the intersection of design, business
Why: Which part of the intersection interests you and what problem you want to learn to address.
Full written prompt: Fashion Design Management sits at the intersection of design, business, culture, and systems. What part of that intersection most interests you right now, and what kind of problem would you like to learn how to address?

Prompt title: Fundamentally, engineering is the application of math, science, and
Why: Why do you want to study engineering.
Full written prompt: Fundamentally, engineering is the application of math, science, and technology to solve complex problems. Why do you want to study engineering?

Prompt title: Please describe why you are interested in being considered for the
Why: Why you want to be considered for one named Cornell programme.
Full written prompt: Please describe why you are interested in being considered for the Brooks School DC Start program.

Prompt title: Submit an artist statement describing your creative interests and
Why: An artist statement plus how studying at Cornell AAP would expand your practice.
Full written prompt: Submit an artist statement describing your creative interests and practice. Address how your work reflects your artistic voice, influences, and process, and how studying art at Cornell AAP would support and expand your practice. (You will also be prompted to upload a copy to your Slideroom portal.)

Prompt title: Tell us about a time you had to make a decision involving competing
Why: A decision with competing priorities, what you decided and what you learned.
Full written prompt: Tell us about a time you had to make a decision involving competing priorities. In the fashion industry, for example, those in the management field are constantly navigating decisions balancing aesthetics and cost, speed and quality, profit and ethics, individual taste and group needs, or creativity and practicality. Your example does not have to relate to fashion because we want to know about your process and how your mind thinks. What did you decide, and what did you learn?

Prompt title: Tell us about something you have made, altered, repaired, styled
Why: Something you made or repaired, the choices and constraints, and what you would change now.
Full written prompt: Tell us about something you have made, altered, repaired, styled, drawn, or imagined. What choices did you make, what constraint di you face, and what would you change if you returned to it now? Formal training is not require; we are interested in your process and how you think.

Prompt title: The College of Human Ecology prepares students to respond to human
Proposed secondaries: Community; Why Major; Why Us; Contribution
Final secondaries: Community; Why Major; Contribution; Why Us
Why: An activity connected to the college mission, what it taught you about community needs, and the impact you can make.
Full written prompt: The College of Human Ecology prepares students to respond to human needs through an education organized around the interconnected issues that profoundly affect individuals, communities, and the institutions that shape our lives. Think about an extracurricular/community engagement/work experience that most closely connects you to the CHE mission and your intended choice of major. Tell us what that experience taught you about your broader community and its needs, and the impact you can make. How will your intended CHE major help you make that impact?

Prompt title: Using your personal, academic, or volunteer/work experiences, describe
Why: Issues you care about, shown to align with the ILR School.
Full written prompt: Using your personal, academic, or volunteer/work experiences, describe the topics or issues that you care about and why they are important to you. Your response should show us that your interests align with the ILR School.

Prompt title: What brings you joy
Why: What brings you joy - filed as Brown's joy prompt is.
Full written prompt: What brings you joy?

Prompt title: What do you believe you will contribute to the Duffield Engineering
Why: What you will contribute to a named campus community and what voice you bring.
Full written prompt: What do you believe you will contribute to the Duffield Engineering community beyond what you've already detailed in your application? What unique voice will you bring?

Prompt title: What draws you to Cornell’s College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Why: What draws you to CALS, across learning, community and impact.
Full written prompt: What draws you to Cornell’s College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS)? Reflect on the learning, community, or impact opportunities that matter most to you, and share how they align with Cornell CALS (as you understand it currently).

Prompt title: What interests you about the major you selected
Why: What interests you about your selected major, via experiences and goals.
Full written prompt: What interests you about the major you selected? Tell us about experiences (both in and outside of the classroom), questions, and goals that influenced your choice.

Prompt title: What is one activity, club, team, organization, work/volunteer
Why: One activity, club, team or family responsibility that is especially meaningful, and its significance - the activity family.
Full written prompt: What is one activity, club, team, organization, work/volunteer experience or family responsibility that is especially meaningful to you? Please briefly tell us about its significance for you.

Prompt title: What is one award you have received or achievement you have attained
Why: One award or achievement that meant the most, and its importance - what came of an involvement.
Full written prompt: What is one award you have received or achievement you have attained that has meant the most to you? Please briefly describe its importance to you.

Prompt title: What kind of business student are you
Why: What kind of business student you are, via issues you care about, aligned to a named school.
Full written prompt: What kind of business student are you? Using your personal, academic, or volunteer/work experiences, describe the topics or issues that you care about and why they are important to you. Your response should convey how your interests align with the school to which you are applying within the Cornell SC Johnson College of Business (the Dyson School or the Nolan School).

Prompt title: Why do you think you would love to study at Duffield Engineering
Why: Why you would love to study at one named college within Cornell.
Full written prompt: Why do you think you would love to study at Duffield Engineering?

Prompt title: Dartmouth fit
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: As you seek admission to Dartmouth's Class of 2031, what aspects of the college's academic program, community, and/or campus environment attract your interest? How is Dartmouth a good fit for you?

Prompt title: Your environment
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: There is a Quaker saying: Let your life speak. Describe the environment in which you were raised and the impact it has had on the person you are today.

Prompt title: Introduce yourself
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: “Be yourself,” Oscar Wilde advised. “Everyone else is taken.” Introduce yourself.

Prompt title: Finding common ground
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: The social and family interactions of wild chimpanzees have been the focus of Dame Jane Goodall's research for decades. Her understanding of animal behavior prompted the English primatologist to see a lesson for human communities as well: “Change happens by listening and then starting a dialogue with the people who are doing something you don't believe is right.” Channel Dame Goodall: Tell us about a moment when you engaged in a difficult conversation or encountered someone with an opinion or perspective that was different from your own. How did you find common ground?

Prompt title: Embracing difference
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: “It’s not easy being green…” was the frequent refrain of Kermit the Frog. How has difference been a part of your life, and how have you embraced it as part of your identity, outlook, or sense of purpose?

Prompt title: What excites you?
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: What excites you?

Prompt title: A life of purpose
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Labor leader and civil rights activist Dolores Huerta recommended a life of purpose. “We must use our lives to make the world a better place to live, not just to acquire things,” she said. “That is what we are put on the earth for.” In what ways do you hope to make—or are you already making—an impact? Why? How?

Prompt title: Celebrate your nerdy side
Why: carried over from the hand review
Full written prompt: Celebrate your nerdy side.
